name: ESP32 DevKitC (WROOM-32)
description: Espressif's ESP32-DevKitC V4 with an ESP32-WROOM-32 module (dual-core Xtensa at 240 MHz, Wi-Fi / Bluetooth not emulated, 4 MB flash), 38 pins, micro-USB with a USB-serial chip (Serial on UART0), BOOT and EN buttons, a power LED but NO user LED. Runs real arduino-esp32 firmware in Espressif's QEMU on your computer (Docker). Pin ids are GPIO numbers. 3.3 V logic only; GPIO34-39 are input-only, GPIO6-11 belong to the flash.

availability.reason: Its fixture test passed on 2026-11-11 (packages/sim-backends/src/qemu-esp/boards.integration.test.ts, board esp32-devkitc): real arduino-esp32 3.3.12 firmware built by Faber's own pipeline boots in Espressif's QEMU; GPIO output, GPIO input with the internal pull-up, and Serial (UART0) reach Faber's parts. Run on the merged jb5 emulator sources (a native QEMU build; the faber/qemu-esp:9.2.2-20260417-jb5 Docker image itself is not built yet). Per-peripheral status: docs/boards.md.

pins.label: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the board's AMS1117 LDO (about 1 V dropout from 5V; Faber checks 500 mA).

pins.label: EN
pins.description: Chip enable / reset (pulled up, the EN button pulls it LOW). Not a GPIO; Faber does not model reset from it.

pins.label: VP/36
pins.description: ESP32 GPIO36; McuBackend pin "GPIO36" (pinMode(36, …) in arduino-esp32). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. SENSOR_VP: INPUT ONLY (no output, no internal pull-up / pull-down). ADC1.

ESP32 GPIO0; McuBackend pin "GPIO0" (pinMode(0, …) in arduino-esp32). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. BOOT button to GND. Strapping pin: LOW at reset = download mode instead of your program. ADC2: analogRead fails while Wi-Fi is on.

ESP32 GPIO2; McuBackend pin "GPIO2" (pinMode(2, …) in arduino-esp32). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Strapping pin: must be LOW or floating to enter download mode. No LED on the DevKitC (some clones have one here). ADC2: analogRead fails while Wi-Fi is on.

ESP32 GPIO15; McuBackend pin "GPIO15" (pinMode(15, …) in arduino-esp32). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Strapping pin (MTDO): LOW at reset silences the boot log; any level boots. ADC2: analogRead fails while Wi-Fi is on.

footprint: 55 × 28 mm, 2 × 19 pins at 0.1 in, rows 0.9 in apart (fits a breadboard with one free row on one side)

bindings.description: Board has power: USB plugged (power.usb) or a supply wired to its power pins keeps the 3.3 V rail up; the firmware is held in reset while false.
True when this board runs the project's firmware (has an MCU backend).
Digital level 0/1 of each GPIO, e.g. pin_GPIO2 (only on the firmware board).

strapping.note: GPIO0 LOW at reset starts the ROM downloader instead of your program (the BOOT button).
GPIO2 must be LOW or floating at reset for flashing; a part pulling it HIGH (an LED to 3V3, a pull-up) makes uploads fail.
GPIO5 sets SDIO slave timing at reset; any level boots.
GPIO12 HIGH at reset selects 1.8 V flash: the WROOM-32 then does not boot (brown-out / flash read errors). Do not pull it up.
GPIO15 LOW at reset only silences the boot log.
